homes.line: The county can charge an impact fee, or use a development agreement, to cover what is needed to handle the impacts its own impact study measures, such as backup power at county facilities.

homes.name: County land lease
homes.line: On land the county owns, the county also sets the rent: cash rent at full market value, with rent paid in kind possible on top.

homes.name: Private agreement
homes.line: Other benefits, such as computing time or training seats, can come only from a private agreement between the developer and a community group. The county is not a party to that agreement.

items.name: Emergency power for county facilities
items.vsub: Only as mitigation the county's impact study supports
items.hnote: Mitigation, sized by the county's impact study. Nothing is delivered from the project site.
items.evText: Model text written; not yet reviewed by a lawyer
items.lead: If the grid goes down for days, the emergency operations center and the other county emergency facilities the county's study names could keep their lights, cooling and radios running. At a shelter, the equipment is sized only for people evacuated because of an incident at the data center, not for hurricane sheltering. The equipment sits at the emergency facility, behind that facility's meter. standards.summary: Standards: what every project must meet
standards.lead: A county does not need any agreement to protect residents. The framework's standards ordinance applies to every large data center, whether or not the developer signs anything, and it asks for no benefits and charges only fees that cover the county's own costs of review and inspection:
standards.numbers: Every number in that ordinance is set by each county from its own studies. The ordinance bars the county from considering any agreement or gift when it decides an application, and from relaxing a standard or speeding up a review because of one (Sec. 16). Where the county keeps an optional rule, a denial may also rest on an uncured default in a mitigation duty under a development agreement the county signed that provides for that remedy, after the notice and cure it requires; such a denial is not reheard on that ground (Sec. 16(e)). Any other decision that considered an agreement or gift is reheard if the applicant or another party asks within the set time and points to the evidence. Choosing not to sign an agreement is a legitimate outcome. Timing: counties covered by a 2025 state law (SB 180 §28) generally cannot propose or adopt new, stricter land rules before 1 Oct 2027.
standards.evidence: Evidence: Drafted. The model ordinance has not been reviewed by a lawyer or adopted anywhere.

groups.note: These are in the model instruments but are not relied on as benefits. Each is a different kind of promise the test does not cover: demand flexibility is mitigation of grid impact, dig-once conduit is a county purchase, colocation is a service the recipient pays for, and the retired-equipment right is a right to buy at fair value. They stay listed so the public can see why.

law.title: What Florida law does not let counties require from a data center
law.count_line: 12 of these apply to data centers.
law.intro: Some items on this page cannot be required by a Florida county because a state law has taken the subject away from counties. A private agreement between the developer and a community group can carry some of them, such as protections for the developer's own workers, because these laws limit counties, not private parties. The county is not part of any such agreement. A single act such as a staff mention likely does not draw it in by itself, but an approval, its terms or its timing that turns on the agreement does (Open Legal Questions, Question 1).
law.describes: It describes; it does not recommend a change.

not_this.title: What this is not
not_this.text: Passing the test only means an item is not ruled out. It does not mean the item is lawful in a given county, wanted by whoever would receive it, agreed to by a developer, or worth a set amount. Each county item still needs its own written link to the impacts in the county's study, a value, and review by the county attorney. A private agreement item needs the community group's own counsel; the county does not review it.

descriptions.title: About the descriptions
descriptions.text: The one-line descriptions and "For your community" notes explain what each item is for. They are not estimates of value. What a resident actually gets depends on who receives the item, the site and the terms agreed.
